rationale: This is essentially the sign-mirrored twin of the archived "Clean Accrual Net Capital Return" (MA3 accrual gap × net financing/payout), differing only by dropping dvc and flipping both legs, so it re-tests an already-evaluated interaction rather than adding new information.

The recch/invch sign correction is handled correctly and the equity-issuance pairing is a defensible variant on the failed debt-funded version, but it remains a straightforward product of two well-known anomalies (working-capital accruals and net share issuance) with limited incremental novelty.

Combining the earnings-minus-cash accrual gap with a genuine debt-maturity-shift leg (Δdlc − Δdltt) is economically coherent, internally consistent in sign, and distinct from both the archived debt-issuance variants and standard published accrual/issuance anomalies.

The expected negative sign conflicts with the payout leg, whose natural direction (buyback/dividend yield, and the archived positive-alpha payout composite) is positive, and the triple rank product neither identifies that payouts are actually debt-funded nor survives the dilution/noise of three multiplied ranks.

This is a cosmetic re-specification of the archived "Continuous Dilution Accrual Deterioration" (csho growth × accrual-gap change) with DELTA swapped for a 3-observation TS_RANK that can take only a handful of coarse values, so it is unlikely to fix the earlier weak result.

Low accruals × net debt retirement is nearly the archived "Clean Accrual Net Capital Return" with the MA(3) smoothing and equity/dividend payout terms stripped out, making it a weaker restatement of an already-tested and already-successful signal rather than a new mechanism.
